> ### Reference · HTML Report Style & Visualization Patterns
> This file is a **reference**, not a rigid specification. Claude should use
> judgment to decide which visualizations, layouts, and styles best serve the
> specific analysis. The patterns below are drawn from proven prior reports and
> provide a starting point — adapt, combine, or omit them as the data demands.

## Report Format: Research Manuscript

The report must read as a **professional research publication**, not a
dashboard or summary card. Structure it like a peer-reviewed systematic
review / meta-analysis manuscript. The expected sections, in order:

1. **Title** — descriptive, specific (intervention, population, design).
2. **Structured abstract** — Background, Methods, Results, Conclusions in
   labeled subsections. Render in a bordered box with small uppercase
   section labels.
3. **Introduction** — context, rationale, and objectives (1-2 paragraphs).
4. **Methods** — search strategy, eligibility criteria, data extraction
   procedure, statistical methods (risk-of-bias tool, effect measures,
   heterogeneity assessment, software). Include PRISMA flow diagram here.
5. **Results** — evidence flow summary, study characteristics overview,
   then per-outcome-group results with forest plots. Each outcome group
   gets its own subsection with a forest plot, pooled estimate, and
   heterogeneity interpretation. Funnel plots for publication bias
   assessment follow when k ≥ 10.
6. **Discussion** — principal findings, comparison with prior evidence,
   heterogeneity interpretation, strengths and limitations.
7. **Conclusions** — brief summary of clinical or practical implications.
8. **Key Findings** — numbered list with certainty ratings (optional but
   recommended for quick-scan readers).
9. **References** — numbered, each linked to the source document via
   `https://citations.gxl.ai`.

Figures (forest plots, funnel plots, PRISMA flow, etc.) should break out
of the reading column into the wider layout, with numbered figure captions
below each.

This is the target quality bar: a reader should be able to cite this report
as they would cite a published systematic review. Every claim is traceable
to an exact source line, every pooled estimate has a visible forest plot,
and the methodology is fully documented.

## Design Principles

The report is a self-contained, static HTML document that reads like a journal
article, not a BI dashboard. Key principles:

- **Minimal and purposeful.** Every visual element earns its place. No
  decorative gradients, shadows, or ornamental borders.
- **Dark mode support.** Use CSS custom properties so the report works in both
  light and dark contexts.
- **Responsive.** Readable on desktop and tablet. Tables and plots scroll
  horizontally on narrow screens.
- **No JavaScript.** The report renders inside a sandboxed iframe that strips
  `<script>`, inline event handlers, and `javascript:` URLs. All interactivity
  comes from `<details>`, `<a>`, and CSS.
- **Self-contained.** Inline CSS only. No external stylesheets, fonts, or
  assets.

## Color Palette (CSS Custom Properties)

Use CSS custom properties for all colors. Example baseline:

```css
:root {
  --bg: #FAFAF8;
  --surface: #FFFFFF;
  --text-primary: #1A1A1A;
  --text-secondary: #6B6B6B;
  --text-muted: #9B9B9B;
  --accent: #B8621B;          /* warm amber; choose per-project */
  --accent-soft: #FEF3E2;
  --border: #E8E8E5;
  --border-soft: #F0F0ED;
  --green: #2F855A;
  --red: #C0392B;
  --reading: 720px;           /* prose column width */
  --wide: 960px;              /* figures/tables breakout width */
}
```

Provide a `[data-theme="dark"]` override block and a
`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback. Dark values:

```css
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg: #161613;
  --surface: #1F1F1C;
  --text-primary: #F2F1ED;
  --text-secondary: #B6B3AC;
  --text-muted: #7D7B74;
  --border: #2F2E2A;
  --border-soft: #262522;
}
```

## Typography

- **Body:** `system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif` at
  17px, line-height 1.65.
- **Headings:** `Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif`, font-weight 400,
  letter-spacing -0.01em. Sizes: h1 44px, h2 28px, h3 21px.
- **Monospace (numbers, CIs):** `"SF Mono", "Fira Code", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`
  at 0.9em.
- **Eyebrow labels:** 12px, letter-spacing 0.12em, uppercase,
  color `var(--accent)`, font-weight 600.
- **Table headers:** 0.72rem, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.05em,
  color `var(--text-muted)`.

## Layout

Two column widths:

- **`.reading`** (max-width 720px): prose, key findings, methods. Centered.
- **`.wide`** (max-width 960px): tables, forest plots, charts. Centered.

Figures that accompany prose should "break out" wider than the reading column
using a `.figure-wide` wrapper (absolute-positioned wider within the centered
column).

## Section Patterns

### Hero / Title Section

Large serif title, a 21px lede paragraph (color `var(--text-secondary)`),
and a grid of stat cards. Stat cards use a grid
(`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))`) and each card shows:

- A small uppercase label (11px, muted)
- A large serif number (32px)
- Optional sub-text (12px, secondary)

### PRISMA / Evidence Flow

Horizontal row of step boxes connected by `→` arrows. Each step box:

- Bordered, rounded (6px), centered text
- Large serif count (26px)
- Small uppercase label below (11px)
- Final step gets `border-color: var(--accent)` and `color: var(--accent)`
  on the count.

Collapses to vertical on narrow screens
(`@media (max-width: 700px) { flex-direction: column; }`).

### Key Findings / Insights

Left border accent cards (3px solid `var(--accent)`) with:

- Small uppercase finding number
- Finding text at 16px
- Optional metadata badges below

### Collapsible Outcome Groups

Use `<details>` with a styled `<summary>` as the outcome header. Each group:

- Header with h3 title + summary stat badges (k=, I²=, pooled estimate)
- Body contains the forest plot SVG, then stats mini-cards, then optional
  funnel plot

## Visualization Reference

Claude decides which visualizations are appropriate based on the data
available and the analysis type. The examples below are patterns that have
worked well — they are not a required checklist.

### Forest Plot (inline SVG)

The most important visualization for pooled analyses. Structure:

- **Three columns:** study label (left, ~360px), plot area (center, ~480px),
  effect + CI text (right, ~160px).
- **Study rows:** 22px row height. Each row shows a label, a horizontal CI
  line, and a square point whose area is proportional to weight.
- **Pooled row:** Diamond polygon below study rows, with bold label + CI text.
- **Null reference line:** Dashed vertical line at the null value (0 for
  differences, 1 for ratios).
- **Axis:** Baseline below pooled row, tick labels, descriptive axis label.
- **Log scale for ratios:** HR, OR, RR use log-scaled x-axis.
- **Color by direction:** Green for favorable direction, red for unfavorable,
  gray when CI crosses null.
- **Clickable study labels:** Each label wraps in `<a>` linking to
  `https://citations.gxl.ai/papers/{doc_id}#{lines}`. CI lines and point
  squares also link. Include link icon (🔗) after label.
- **Tooltips:** `<title>` elements on squares showing study name, effect,
  CI, and weight %.
- **Imputed CIs:** Dashed CI lines with lower opacity; mark with `†` in the
  CI text column.
- **Legend:** Below axis: "Click any study to view the source passage in
  context."

Key sizing:
```
viewBox: 0 0 1000 {dynamic_height}
row_h = 22, header_h = 28, pooled_row_h = 36, axis_h = 36
label font: 11px system-ui  |  CI font: 11px monospace  |  axis: 10px
```

Point square sizing: `size = min(14, max(6, 6 + 8 * (weight / max_weight)))`.

### Funnel Plot (inline SVG)

For assessing publication bias:

- Inverted y-axis (SE, large at bottom).
- Dashed pooled estimate vertical line in accent color.
- Dashed 95% pseudo-CI funnel (1.96 × SE envelope).
- Study points as filled circles (r=3.5), with `<title>` tooltips.
- Trim-and-fill imputed points as open circles in accent color.
- Egger's p-value text in top-right corner when available.
- Axis labels: "Effect size" or "Effect (log scale)" on x-axis,
  "Standard error" on y-axis (rotated).
- Typical size: 480 × 360.

### Risk-of-Bias Traffic Light (inline SVG)

For domain-level quality assessment:

- Grid of colored circles: green (low), amber (some concerns), red (high),
  gray (not assessed).
- Study labels on the left (clickable to source), domain names rotated at
  top.
- Cell size ~30px, label column ~220px.

### Network Diagram (inline SVG)

For network meta-analyses:

- Circular node layout with edge lines.
- Node radius proportional to sample size, edge width proportional to
  number of studies.
- Labels below nodes.
- Typical size: 420 × 420.

### Other Diagnostic Charts

These are useful when the analysis data supports them. All follow the same
SVG pattern: no JavaScript, axis labels, tooltips via `<title>`, citation
links on data points when `doc_id` is available.

- **Cumulative meta-analysis:** Shows how the pooled estimate changes as
  studies are added chronologically. Horizontal CI lines with dots,
  label column on left.
- **Meta-regression:** Scatter plot with optional regression line (dashed).
  Bubble size by weight.
- **L'Abbé plot:** Control vs. treatment event rates. Diagonal reference
  line at equality.
- **Galbraith / radial plot:** Precision (1/SE) on x-axis, standardized
  effect (z) on y-axis. ±2 reference lines.
- **Dose-response curve:** Connected line with CI whiskers.
- **Saturation curve:** Evidence accumulation over time.

### Summary Statistics Mini-Cards

Grid of small stat boxes (`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr))`),
each showing:

- Small uppercase label (0.68rem, muted)
- Large value (1.1rem serif, bold)
- Optional sub-text

Use these to display per-outcome-group stats like k, I², τ², prediction
interval, and Egger's p alongside forest plots.

### GRADE Summary-of-Findings Table

When certainty assessments are available:

| Outcome | Studies | Participants | Effect (95% CI) | Certainty | Summary |
|---------|---------|-------------|-----------------|-----------|---------|

Certainty badges use filled dots: ●●●● High, ●●●○ Moderate, ●●○○ Low,
●○○○ Very Low. Color-coded by level.

## Citation Links

Every source-backed value in the report should link to the original passage.
The URL format is:

```
https://citations.gxl.ai/papers/{doc_id}#{lines}
```

Where `{lines}` uses the `L` prefix format: `L45`, `L45-L52`, or
`L45,L120,L210`.

In forest plots and other SVG charts, wrap study labels and data marks in
`<a href="..." target="_blank" rel="noopener">`. In HTML tables and prose,
use standard anchor tags.

DOI fallback (`https://doi.org/{doi}`) when no Paperclip document ID exists.

## Tables

- Full width, collapsed borders, 0.9rem font.
- Headers: sticky top, uppercase, muted color, clickable for sort
  (CSS-only via `<details>` pattern or pre-sorted sections).
- Row hover: `background: var(--accent-soft)`.
- Numeric columns: right-aligned with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
- Alternating row tints are optional; hover highlight is primary.

## Render QA Invariants

The current machine gate distinguishes hard failures from warnings.

**Hard failures (exit nonzero, `render_qa.json.status:"fail"`):**

1. invalid readable `report_spec.json` when present;
2. JavaScript/handlers/iframes or content changed by sandbox sanitization;
3. empty tables, SVGs, forest plots, or `chart-*` SVGs with axes but no data;
4. no citation links, or a forest with study rows but no citation link;
5. a literal sentinel as an element's value: `None`, `NaN`, `undefined`,
   `null`, or `N/A` (case-insensitive); render missing data as `—`;
6. an identified forest whose count of `data-study` markers differs from the
   uniquely matched managed pairwise outcome's pooled `k`;
7. a visible figure ID declared by `report_spec.json` or
   `dashboard_spec.json` that is absent from `index.html` or has no rendered
   table data, media, or SVG data marks;
8. missing `<h1>`, missing References, or zero rendered forests when synthesis
   explicitly declares forest figures; and
9. HTML size at or above 25 MB.

**Warnings (the machine status may still be `pass`):**

- `report_spec.json` absent on a legacy invocation;
- unreadable `dashboard_spec.json`;
- GXL citation links without exact `#L...` anchors, including links whose
  managed analysis row has lines available;
- forest plots with missing/ambiguous stable outcome identifiers, fewer
  forests than poolable pairwise groups, or fewer than synthesis declares;
- skipped normalization/parity checks; and
- missing viewport metadata.

Forest row validation is active only when a forest has one stable identifier
that uniquely matches a managed pairwise group. Put a stable `data-outcome`
(or `data-outcome-id`) on the forest SVG/container, and put exactly one
`data-study="<stable study/card id>"` marker inside the forest for each study
counted by pooled `k`. An unassociated forest warns; an associated `k` mismatch
is hard.

Visible-figure validation is also active. Every visible figure declaration must
have a stable ID, and `index.html` must contain a populated element whose HTML
`id` exactly equals that declaration. Use `data-figure-id` in addition when
helpful, but it does not replace the exact DOM `id`.

## Full Example: Forest Plot SVG Structure

This is a simplified reference for the SVG structure. Adapt dimensions,
colors, and content to the analysis.

```html
<figure id="forest-{outcome_id}" data-figure-id="forest-{outcome_id}"
        data-outcome="{outcome_id}">
<div class="forest-wrapper">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1000 {height}" class="forest-plot"
     data-outcome="{outcome_id}"
     preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin meet"
     role="img" aria-label="Forest plot for {outcome}">
  <defs><style>
    .fp-label { font: 11px system-ui, sans-serif; fill: #1A1A1A }
    .fp-ci-text { font: 11px monospace; fill: #6B6B6B }
    .fp-axis-text { font: 10px system-ui, sans-serif; fill: #6B6B6B }
    .fp-link { cursor: pointer }
    .fp-link:hover .fp-label { fill: var(--accent) }
  </style></defs>

  <!-- Column headers -->
  <text x="8" y="18" class="fp-label" font-weight="600">Study</text>
  <text x="848" y="18" class="fp-label" font-weight="600">
    Effect [95% CI]
  </text>

  <!-- Null reference line (dashed) -->
  <line x1="600" y1="28" x2="600" y2="{bottom}"
        stroke="#9B9B9B" stroke-dasharray="2,2"/>

  <!-- Per-study row: linked label + CI line + weighted square -->
  <a href="https://citations.gxl.ai/papers/PMC123#L45"
     target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="fp-link">
    <text x="8" y="42" class="fp-label">
      Author et al (2024) 🔗
    </text>
    <line x1="520" y1="39" x2="680" y2="39"
          stroke="#0E8A55" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <rect data-study="{stable_study_or_card_id}"
          x="596" y="33" width="10" height="10" fill="#0E8A55">
      <title>Author et al: 0.85 [0.72, 0.95], w=12.3%</title>
    </rect>
  </a>
  <text x="848" y="42" class="fp-ci-text">0.85 [0.72, 0.95]</text>

  <!-- Pooled diamond -->
  <polygon points="510,{py} 600,{py-8} 690,{py} 600,{py+8}"
           fill="var(--accent)" stroke="var(--accent)">
    <title>Pooled (REML+KH): 0.82 [0.71, 0.90]</title>
  </polygon>
  <text x="8" y="{py+3}" class="fp-label" font-weight="600">
    Pooled (REML+KH)
  </text>

  <!-- Axis -->
  <line x1="360" y1="{bottom}" x2="840" y2="{bottom}"
        stroke="#1A1A1A"/>
  <text x="600" y="{bottom+28}" class="fp-axis-text"
        text-anchor="middle">
    Effect size — null at 0
  </text>

  <!-- Legend -->
  <text x="360" y="{height-10}" class="fp-legend"
        style="font:10px system-ui;fill:#9B9B9B">
    Click any study to view the source passage in context
  </text>
</svg>
</div>
<figcaption>Figure N. Forest plot for {outcome}.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## Full Example: PRISMA Flow

```html
<div class="prisma-flow">
  <div class="prisma-step">
    <span class="count">2,847</span>
    <span class="label">Indexed</span>
  </div>
  <span class="prisma-arrow">→</span>
  <div class="prisma-step">
    <span class="count">312</span>
    <span class="label">Screened</span>
  </div>
  <span class="prisma-arrow">→</span>
  <div class="prisma-step">
    <span class="count">89</span>
    <span class="label">Full-text</span>
  </div>
  <span class="prisma-arrow">→</span>
  <div class="prisma-step" style="border-color:var(--accent)">
    <span class="count" style="color:var(--accent)">39</span>
    <span class="label">Included</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Choosing Visualizations

The data determines what to show. Common mappings:

| Data available | Suggested visualization |
|---------------|------------------------|
| Outcome groups with studies + CIs | Forest plot per group |
| Studies with SE + effect | Funnel plot (≥3 studies) |
| Per-domain quality ratings | Risk-of-bias traffic light |
| Multiple interventions compared | Network diagram |
| Chronological study accumulation | Cumulative meta-analysis |
| Continuous moderator + effect | Meta-regression scatter |
| Control + treatment rates | L'Abbé plot |
| Certainty/GRADE assessments | Summary-of-findings table |
| Search/screening counts | PRISMA flow diagram |

Include a visualization only when the data is populated. An empty chart frame
is worse than no chart. The render QA enforces this: every declared SVG must
contain data marks, not just axes and labels.
